hints.title: Record what a valid path requires
hints.body: After any initial part of a valid code, the number of U steps is at least the number of D steps. At the end their numbers are equal.
hints.recap: Every partial height is nonnegative; the final height is zero.
hints.pitfall: Equal total numbers of U and D do not alone make a code valid.
hints.pause: What must the first and last letters of a nonempty valid code be?

recall.reminder: Check every condition in the definition, not just one part.

hints.title: Track the transformed first step
hints.body: For reversal, the old last letter becomes the first. For the letter interchange, the old first letter changes type. Compare those new starts with the nonnegative-height condition.
hints.recap: A single forbidden partial height refutes validity.
hints.pitfall: Total balance alone is not enough.
hints.pause: Assess the first two transformations against the initial-height requirement.

recall.reminder: A single forbidden partial height refutes validity.

hints.title: Check the enclosed old path
hints.body: For the added initial and final steps, track how the middle path’s heights change, then check its final height and the total numbers of each step.
hints.recap: Every partial height and the final balance both matter.
hints.pitfall: Do not check only the extra first step.
hints.pause: Prove or refute validity of the third transformation and combine your classifications.

recall.reminder: Every partial height and the final balance both matter.

solution:
For a valid nonempty code, the first letter must be U; otherwise the path immediately drops below sea level. The last letter must be D; ending with U would require the preceding height to be −1 in order to finish at zero.

Reversal therefore starts with D, so I is false. Interchanging U and D also changes the initial U into D, so II is false.

For III, the added initial U lifts every point of the original path by one unit. The middle section never drops below height 1, ends at height 1, and the final D returns to zero. There are n+1 steps of each type, so the result is a valid profile.

Answer D: III only.
